headline: Web and database tools link structure, bioactivity and genome data to candidate peptides
label: Computational Peptide Discovery Tools
summary: Recent preprints and DBAASP V4 couple structure prediction and curated bioactivity records to candidate-level outputs.
synthesis: The studies share a tooling orientation rather than a single method. DBAASP V4 links peptides and peptidomimetics to condition-resolved antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer and cytotoxicity data. ToxINsight curates 2,078 snake venom toxin entries with 2,540 3D structures and offers alignment and ligand binding analysis. Peptorama draws non-ribosomal peptide structures and compares known and BGC-predicted NRPs at the peptide level. A leech salivary-EV study applies ESMFold and Foldseek/TM-align to assign a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger fold and flags a structurally dark fraction. Roost integrates avian influenza publications, surveillance detections and avian genome assemblies using LLM-assisted literature processing. The dominant thread is infrastructure that connects structural prediction, curated bioactivity data and sequence or genome-derived candidates into outputs usable for selection. The leech study is a single-protein annotation and does not itself provide a platform.
